_meta.description: Cammelot Living Patient Agent — persona archetype library. Each archetype is an authored 'character genome' that gives a citizen a distinct voice, temperament, and behavioral parameters. Citizens are matched to an archetype at spawn (deterministic, seeded) and receive small per-citizen jitter so no two are identical. Behavioral params drive care-seeking, compliance, refusal, and second-opinion behavior in the deterministic engine; thought templates replace the old generic generateThoughts() flavor lines. The disease (Markov) engine is unaffected.

behaviorParamGuide.careSeekingBias: -0.5..0.5. Negative = waits longer before seeking care (higher tolerance for HP loss). Positive = seeks care early.
behaviorParamGuide.compliance: 0..1. Likelihood to follow treatment advice and remain in a queue rather than abandon it.
behaviorParamGuide.trustInSystem: 0..1. Belief the system will help. Low trust raises refusal/second-opinion tendencies.
behaviorParamGuide.refusalTendency: 0..1. Probability of abandoning a queue once the wait is clearly overdue (Treeknorm breached).
behaviorParamGuide.secondOpinionDrive: 0..1. Probability of seeking an alternative provider after a disappointing encounter.
behaviorParamGuide.drainModifier: 0.85..1.15. Multiplier on HP drain from waiting; optimism/resilience < 1, anxiety/fatalism > 1.
behaviorParamGuide.socialness: 0..1. Tendency to chat with neighbours and propagate town sentiment.

archetypes.label: The Stoic Old Hand
archetypes.voice: Terse, understated, proud. Distrusts fuss and self-pity. 'De dokter weet het best.'

healthy: Work to do. No time to be ill.
A walk does more than any pill.
The garden won't tend itself.
early_symptoms: It's nothing. It'll pass.
I've felt worse and carried on.
No sense bothering the doctor over this.
waiting: You wait your turn. That's how it is.
Others have it worse than me.
Patience. The appointment will come.
long_wait: Long enough now. But complaining changes nothing.
I'll not make a scene about it.
A man waits. Even when it's wrong.
declining: Body's giving out. So it goes.
I won't pretend it's fine. But I won't whine either.
Should have gone in sooner, perhaps.
treated: Good. Now let me get on with things.
The doctor did her job. Fair enough.
Sorted. Back to the garden.
recovering: Mending slowly. As it should.
Bit by bit. No rushing it.
Stronger than last week. That's enough.
grief: A good neighbour, gone. That's the way of it.
We bury our own and carry on.
I'll not say much. But I felt it.

archetypes.label: The Anxious Caregiver
archetypes.voice: Worried, vigilant, protective. Catastrophizes quietly. Has people depending on her.

healthy: Everyone's fed and well. For now.
I should book that check-up I keep putting off.
Is that a new ache, or am I imagining it?
early_symptoms: What if this is something serious?
I can't afford to be sick. The kids need me.
I'm calling the practice first thing tomorrow.
waiting: Why haven't they called yet?
Every day waiting is a day it could get worse.
I keep rehearsing what I'll tell the doctor.
long_wait: This wait is making me ill with worry.
I read about someone who waited too long. I can't stop thinking about it.
Maybe I should try a different clinic.
declining: It's getting worse and no one is listening.
I knew it. I knew I should have pushed harder.
Who will look after them if I can't?
treated: Finally. Some relief. I can breathe.
Thank god someone took it seriously.
I'll follow every instruction to the letter.
recovering: Slowly better. I'm almost afraid to believe it.
I'm watching every symptom like a hawk.
One good week. Please let there be another.
grief: That could have been any of us. It terrifies me.
I can't stop thinking about their family.
I'm holding mine a little closer tonight.

archetypes.label: The Stubborn Skeptic
archetypes.voice: Distrustful of institutions, blunt, independent. Has been let down before.

healthy: I manage my own health, thanks.
Doctors. Always something with them.
Feeling fine. Don't need anyone telling me otherwise.
early_symptoms: I'll deal with it myself.
Half their 'treatments' are nonsense anyway.
Not running to the GP for every little thing.
waiting: Knew they'd make me wait. They always do.
This is exactly why I don't bother with them.
A number in a queue. That's all we are to them.
long_wait: The system doesn't care about people like me.
Twelve weeks. And they call this care.
I've half a mind to walk out and forget it.
declining: So much for their wonderful system.
Should've trusted my gut and gone private.
They let it get this far. Typical.
treated: About time. Won't be thanking anyone.
Fine. It worked. Doesn't change what I think.
One decent doctor in the whole lot.
recovering: Getting better. No thanks to the wait.
I'll take the recovery. Keep the lectures.
Back on my feet. On my own terms.
grief: The system failed them. I won't pretend otherwise.
Another one the waiting list killed.
Makes my blood boil, that does.

archetypes.label: The Sunny Optimist
archetypes.voice: Warm, hopeful, resilient. Finds the bright side, sometimes to a fault.

healthy: What a morning to be alive!
Think I'll bring the neighbours some cake.
Life's good. Mustn't forget to say so.
early_symptoms: Probably nothing — but better safe than sorry.
I'll get it checked and put my mind at ease.
A small bump. We'll sort it out.
waiting: They'll get to me soon, I'm sure.
Good things to those who wait, they say.
I'll use the time to rest up properly.
long_wait: It's a long wait, but I trust it'll come good.
Worrying won't speed it up. Best stay cheerful.
I've got my appointment circled. Almost there.
declining: A rough patch. We all have them.
I'll lean on my friends and get through it.
Down today. Up tomorrow, hopefully.
treated: See? It all worked out in the end!
What a relief. I knew it would be alright.
I could hug that doctor.
recovering: Stronger every single day!
The sun's out and so am I, nearly.
Soon I'll be back to my old self.
grief: I'll remember the good times we shared.
A sad day. We'll look after each other.
Let's celebrate the life, not just mourn it.

archetypes.label: The Weary Chronic Patient
archetypes.voice: Resigned, knowledgeable about her own illness, tired of the routine but compliant.

healthy: A quiet day. I'll take it.
Pills sorted, walk done. Routine keeps me steady.
No news from the body. That's good news.
early_symptoms: I know this feeling. Here we go again.
Best log it and ring the practice.
My body and I have been here before.
waiting: Same queue, different season.
I know the drill. Bring a book.
Waiting is half my life with this condition.
long_wait: Tired of waiting, but what can you do.
The condition doesn't wait, even if the clinic does.
Another long stretch. I'll manage. I always do.
declining: I can feel it slipping. I know the signs.
This is the part I dread.
I've fought this a long time. I'm weary.
treated: Adjusted my meds. Back to managing.
The specialist knows my history. That helps.
Patched up for another stretch.
recovering: Steadier now. Small mercies.
Back to my routine. It's a comfort, really.
The good days are quieter. I'm grateful for them.
grief: I knew their illness too. Could've been me.
We chronic ones look out for each other.
One fewer at the clinic now. It stings.

archetypes.label: The Busy Professional
archetypes.voice: Time-pressed, pragmatic, efficiency-minded. Health is a logistics problem to be solved.

healthy: Booked back-to-back. No time to be ill.
I'll deal with it on the weekend. Maybe.
Health's fine. It's the calendar that's sick.
early_symptoms: Can I push this to next week?
I'll take something and power through.
If it's quick, I'll see someone. If not, it waits.
waiting: This wait is costing me actual work hours.
Surely there's a faster route through this.
I'll chase them. Squeaky wheel and all that.
long_wait: This is absurdly inefficient. Someone should fix it.
I'd pay to skip this queue, frankly.
Three months? I could've flown abroad and back.
declining: I let this slide too long. Bad call.
Can't optimize my way out of this one.
Note to self: don't ignore the body's deadlines.
treated: Good. Done. Next problem.
Efficient, finally. That's all I wanted.
Crossed off the list. Onward.
recovering: Back to capacity, nearly.
Productivity returning. Good.
Lesson logged. Won't repeat the mistake.
grief: Puts the deadlines in perspective, doesn't it.
We never think we'll run out of time.
I'll send the family something. The least I can do.

archetypes.label: The Lonely Elder
archetypes.voice: Gentle, isolated, values the human contact of a visit as much as the care itself.

healthy: The clinic ladies always have a kind word.
Bit quiet at home. A walk into town does me good.
I do like a chat at the pharmacy.
early_symptoms: At least it gives me a reason to see someone.
I'll mention it when I go in. Nice to be seen.
Company and a check-up. Two birds.
waiting: I don't mind the waiting room. People to watch.
They know me by name now, the receptionists.
Bit of a wait, but the bus ride out is pleasant.
long_wait: It's a long time to be on my own with it.
I worry, but I've no one to say it to.
The days feel longer when you're waiting alone.
declining: I don't want to be a bother to anyone.
If only someone could come and sit a while.
It's the being alone with it that's hardest.
treated: The nurse held my hand. I'll not forget it.
So good to be cared for. Truly.
A bit of kindness goes a long way at my age.
recovering: Feeling brighter. And I had a lovely chat too.
Mending — and the company helped as much as the pills.
Back on my feet, and back to my little routines.
grief: Another friend gone. The circle gets smaller.
We used to wait in that room together.
I'll miss our chats more than I can say.

archetypes.label: The Young Invincible
archetypes.voice: Carefree, dismissive of illness, believes bad things happen to other people.

healthy: Young, free, and feeling great.
Doctors are for old people, basically.
Nothing's going to slow me down.
early_symptoms: I'll sleep it off. Always works.
It's nothing. I'm nineteen, come on.
Can't be bothered with the GP for this.
waiting: Wait, why am I even in this queue?
I'll probably be fine before they call me.
This is eating into my whole day.
long_wait: Honestly might just forget the appointment.
Still here? It can't be that serious.
I've better things to do than wait around.
declining: Okay, this is actually not great.
Maybe I should've taken it seriously.
Didn't think it'd get to this. Huh.
treated: Sorted. Back to normal, then.
See, knew it'd be fine.
Right, never doing that again. Probably.
recovering: Bouncing back already. Told you.
Good as new, basically.
Lesson learned. For about a week.
grief: That's... genuinely shaken me up.
You never think it's real until it is.
Makes you feel weirdly fragile, that.

archetypes.label: The Informed Advocate
archetypes.voice: Reads everything, knows the Treeknorm, advocates for himself and others. Demanding but fair.

healthy: Knowledge is the best medicine, I always say.
I keep my own records. You have to.
Prevention beats cure. The data is clear.
early_symptoms: I've read the guidelines. This warrants a visit.
I know which questions to ask.
Catching it early changes everything. Let's go.
waiting: This wait is approaching the Treeknorm limit.
I'll be quoting the norms if this drags on.
I'm tracking exactly how long this takes.
long_wait: This breaches the Treeknorm. That's not acceptable.
I'll escalate. And I'll help others do the same.
The norm says four weeks. We're well past that.
declining: This decline was preventable. I'll document it.
The delay caused this. I want it on record.
I did everything right. The system didn't.
treated: Good clinical care, once I finally reached it.
I'll give credit where it's due. The doctor was excellent.
Treated well. The pathway to get here was the problem.
recovering: Recovering, and writing it all up for the next person.
On the mend. Now to fix the queue that nearly cost me.
Better. And better informed than ever.
grief: A preventable death. The numbers will show it.
This is what waiting lists do. We must say so.
I'll make sure their story isn't just a statistic.

archetypes.label: The Quiet Fatalist
archetypes.voice: Melancholic, accepting of decline, low expectations of help. Withdrawn.

healthy: Quiet day. They're all much the same.
No complaints. None that matter, anyway.
You take what comes. That's all there is.
early_symptoms: What will be, will be.
No point making a fuss over it.
These things run their course regardless.
waiting: I expected the wait. I expect most things.
They'll get to me or they won't.
I've stopped hoping it'll be quick.
long_wait: Of course it's a long wait. It always is.
I won't chase them. What would be the use.
The waiting is just how it ends, isn't it.
declining: I saw this coming. I always do.
It is what it was always going to be.
No surprises here. Just the slow part.
treated: Well. That's more than I expected.
Help, for once. I'll not get used to it.
Patched up. We'll see how long it holds.
recovering: A reprieve, I suppose. For now.
Better, against my expectations.
I'll take the quiet while it lasts.
grief: We all go the same way in the end.
I felt it coming for them. As I do for myself.
One less of us. Soon enough, the rest.

archetypes.label: The Cheerful Grandparent
archetypes.voice: Generous, community-minded, full of stories. Health worries hidden behind a smile.

healthy: The grandchildren are coming Sunday. Bliss.
I baked too much again. Who wants some?
A good life, all told. Can't complain.
early_symptoms: I'll get it seen to. Mustn't worry the family.
Best stay well for the little ones.
A quick visit and I'll be right as rain.
waiting: I'll knit something while I wait.
Plenty of folk to talk to in that room.
The wait's no trouble. I've stories to tell.
long_wait: I keep it cheerful, but it has been a while.
I don't want the family fretting over me.
A long wait. I'll not let it dim my spirits.
declining: I put on a brave face for the little ones.
I don't want to be a worry to anyone.
It's harder than I let on, truth be told.
treated: Right as rain! Now, who wants cake?
The doctor was a dear. Lovely girl.
Sorted, and just in time for Sunday.
recovering: Getting my strength back for the grandchildren.
Better every day — and the visits help!
Soon I'll be chasing the little ones again.
grief: A dear old friend. We shared so many years.
I'll bring the family something warm. We grieve together.
So many stories go with them. I'll tell them still.

archetypes.label: The Overwhelmed Young Parent
archetypes.voice: Stretched thin, sleep-deprived, puts everyone else's health before her own.

healthy: Everyone's healthy. I'll worry about me later.
No time to be tired. There's too much to do.
If the kids are well, I'm well. Sort of.
early_symptoms: I haven't got time to be ill right now.
I'll push through. I always do.
Maybe if I just ignore it, it'll go.
waiting: I can't take another afternoon off for this.
Who's watching the kids while I wait here?
Every hour in this queue is an hour I don't have.
long_wait: I can't keep rearranging my whole life around this.
I'm running on empty and still waiting.
I should chase it, but who has the energy.
declining: I left it too long. I always leave it too long.
I can't fall apart. They need me upright.
If I go down, the whole house goes with me.
treated: Okay. Okay. One less thing to carry.
Finally sorted. Now back to the chaos.
Relief. I didn't realize how scared I was.
recovering: Bit more energy today. Thank goodness.
Getting there — between school runs.
Better. The house can breathe again.
grief: It makes me hold the children tighter.
I can't imagine. Their poor family.
Life's so fragile. And I'm so tired.

archetypes.label: The Proud Independent
archetypes.voice: Fiercely self-reliant, hates asking for help, equates illness with weakness.

healthy: I've never needed anyone's help and I never will.
Stand on your own feet. That's how I was raised.
Fit as a fiddle. I see to that myself.
early_symptoms: I'll sort myself out. I always have.
No need to trouble the doctor with this.
A bit of grit and it'll pass.
waiting: I don't like sitting here, hat in hand.
Asking for help never sat right with me.
I'd rather manage it alone, if I could.
long_wait: Hate to admit it, but I might need them after all.
Galling, this. Waiting on others.
I'll not beg. But it's wearing me down.
declining: I should have asked sooner. Pride's a poor doctor.
Hard to admit I can't manage this one alone.
Even I have to bend, it seems.
treated: There. Sorted. I'll manage from here myself.
Took help. Just this once.
Back in charge of my own affairs now.
recovering: On my own two feet again. As it should be.
Don't need fussing over. I'm mending fine.
Independence restored. Good.
grief: A proud one, like me. Went their own way.
I respect how they carried it. Alone, mostly.
We don't say much, our sort. But I feel it.

archetypes.label: The Curious Child
archetypes.voice: Innocent, literal, frightened of the unfamiliar but quick to bounce back. Relies on parents.

healthy: Can we go to the park after?
I drew a picture of our house!
I'm not tired, I promise I'm not.
early_symptoms: My tummy feels funny.
Do I have to see the doctor? I don't want a needle.
Mum, I don't feel right.
waiting: Is it our turn yet? Is it now?
The waiting room has a fish tank!
I'm bored. How much longer?
long_wait: We've been here aaaages.
Why does it take so long, Mum?
I want to go home now.
declining: I feel really poorly.
I don't like feeling like this.
Make it stop, please.
treated: The doctor gave me a sticker!
That wasn't so bad after all.
I was brave, wasn't I?
recovering: I feel much better now! Can I play?
Can I have ice cream because I was poorly?
I'm all better! Watch me run!
grief: Where did they go? Are they coming back?
Mum looks sad. I gave her a hug.
I don't really understand, but I feel sad too.

archetypes.label: The Idealistic Teen
archetypes.voice: Passionate, justice-minded, distrusts authority but cares deeply. Dramatic, sincere.

healthy: The world's a mess but today's actually alright.
I'm fine. Stop asking, honestly.
Me and my friends are gonna change everything.
early_symptoms: It's probably nothing. I don't want a big deal made.
I'll tell someone if it gets worse. Maybe.
Ugh, I do not have time to be sick.
waiting: This wait is so unfair. People are suffering.
Why is the system like this? It's broken.
Someone should do something about these queues.
long_wait: This is exactly what's wrong with everything.
People my gran's age are waiting months. It's wrong.
I'm going to post about how broken this is.
declining: This shouldn't be happening to anyone.
I'm scared but I don't want to show it.
It's not fair. None of this is fair.
treated: Okay, that doctor actually really cared. Respect.
Maybe the people are good even if the system's bad.
Relieved. And kind of grateful, honestly.
recovering: Feeling better. Back to changing the world.
Stronger now. And more fired up than ever.
I'm okay — but I won't forget how it felt.
grief: This is what the waiting lists do. It's a scandal.
I won't let them be just a number.
I'm angry and sad and I want it to mean something.

archetypes.label: The Gentle Homemaker
archetypes.voice: Soft-spoken, nurturing, routine-loving. Trusts gradual care and home remedies first.

healthy: Soup's on, washing's out. A good day.
A warm house and good health. What more.
I like the quiet rhythm of an ordinary day.
early_symptoms: A bit of rest and some broth first, I think.
I'll see how it sits for a day or two.
Honey and lemon before anything drastic.
waiting: I'll keep busy at home while I wait.
No use fretting. The kettle's always on.
I'll tend the house and let it take its time.
long_wait: It's a long wait. I'll keep things ticking over.
I worry a little, but I keep it gentle.
The home keeps me steady through the waiting.
declining: I'm finding it harder to keep up with things.
The house feels heavier than it used to.
I don't like to complain, but I am struggling.
treated: Such a relief. Back to my little routines.
The doctor was so kind and patient.
I can put the kettle on with an easy mind now.
recovering: A bit stronger each day. The house helps.
Slowly back to my rhythm. It's a comfort.
Mending gently, just the way I like.
grief: I'll bring their family a warm meal.
Such a kind soul. The street feels emptier.
We hold each other up at times like these.
